assign.request: Design a CSSDoc system: metadata per CSS selector/rule, with the live rule pulled from the stylesheet and parsed by the browser.
assign.now: briefing an Opus minion on the design

log.msg: measured the CSSOM on /framework/ext/Doc/ headless: 72 stylesheets (58 link, 14 style), 1316 style rules, 86 @layer blocks, 27 @media, 10 @container, 0 @import, 0 cross-origin failures. Exactly 8 of the 1316 land on a pre > code. The filter is the whole product.

SMOKING GUN: /framework/styles/elements/code/ already exists and its stated job is the element rendered beside the rule that styles it. Four of its hand-copied CSS quotes are wrong against the live sheet, including pre > code missing box-shadow: none - the exact declaration tonight fixed. Same failure mode as files:, but the declarations ARE available at runtime.

Traps verified, not asserted: el.matches(code::before) returns false and NEVER throws, so a naive matcher silently loses every pseudo-element rule. 14 of 72 sheets have no href at all (ui/parts.js appends a bare style tag with zero attributes). No line-number API exists on a rule, and cssText is normalised (*, *::before, *::after becomes *, ::before, ::after), so grepping the source for it is unreliable too.

Best finding: no specificity API is needed. getComputedStyle on a live specimen IS the resolved cascade. box-shadow on the block reads none (two rules) and on the inline reads rgb(230,230,230) 0 0 0 1px inset (one rule) - the defect is a diff between two specimens in one table. Also measured: the browser DROPS declarations it cannot parse (color: reed and wibble: 3 vanish), so a typo appears as a missing row.

proposal.md landed, 173 lines. Verdicts: (1) ext/CSSDoc exporting cssdoc(target) as a BLOCK, not a Doc tab - every page under /framework/styles/ is a plain Page, so a Doc section would reach none of them; (2) the unit is a TARGET, not a selector - one rule (pre, code, kbd, samp, .code) belongs to five targets and has no single file; (3) walk + recurse grouping rules, getComputedStyle names the winner; (4) doc/style/<name>.md from css-scopes.txt, a selector is a row and an anchor, never a filename; (5) live specimen, generated rule table, property table, then prose. v1 = one file, one call site, one subject.

proposal ACCEPTED, all five verdicts. Decisive evidence: /framework/styles/elements/code/ already exists and four of its hand-copied rules are wrong, missing exactly the box-shadow: none that tonight's defect was. Commissioning v1 build.

assign.now: building CSSDoc v1 — cssdoc(target) block, subject: code

log.msg: NEGATIVE RESULT, and it strengthens the design: a static linter cannot find tonight's bug class. Three passes over the live CSSOM (1316 rules) hunting 'contextual rule that nulls some of its base's properties but not all' gave 149, then 74, then 12 candidates — every survivor was an INTENTIONAL override (.dt-spot.dt-up repositions a tag; it should not restate padding). What made pre>code a defect was intent — the reset was meant to neutralise the whole inline chip look, and box-shadow was part of that look. Intent is not in the CSSOM. Only seeing BOTH renderings beside one property table exposes it, which is exactly cssdoc(). Do not build the linter.

anonymous-sheets.md written: ui/parts.js css() appends a bare <style>, so 14 of 72 sheets cannot name their file. The fix is one optional arg BUT 34 caller files = CLAUDE.md 'ask before major surgery'. Left as a proposal with a recommendation to do nothing for now.

agent.outcome: ACCEPTED — five verdicts, all measured; found /framework/styles/elements/code/ already exists with four wrong hand-copied rules

log.msg: ACCEPTANCE TEST PASSES at 400/1280/1920/3440, zero console errors. The box-shadow row, verbatim: 'box-shadow | rgb(230, 230, 230) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset | code | none | code · pre > code' - one rule on the inline specimen, two on the block. The pre > code rule row, verbatim: '34 | theme | framework.css | pre > code | padding: 0px; background: none; box-shadow: none; | block'. 8 rules out of 1305 land on code; 20 property rows; 7 of them marked as a diff between the two specimens.

MOUNT SEAM: there is no post-mount hook a block can reach. Page.activate() calls activated() but that fires while App.$app is still DETACHED on a cold load (inject() runs after await this.load()), so activated(), queueMicrotask and Page.render() are all too early - the a11y note in core/new/1 says the same thing about isConnected being false exactly once. Used the two real preconditions instead: Promise.allSettled(View.stylesheets) then a MutationObserver on document.documentElement until el.isConnected. Never rAF - a hidden tab does not animate and MCP eval always runs in one. PROOF: the block stamps data-connected on itself at measure time and headless reads 'true' at all four widths; a detached code element measures getComputedStyle(el).boxShadow === '' (verified).

A FIFTH wrong hand-typed CSS claim, found by the new block and measured: the tokens demo captioned itself 'Inline code and the block below both retune' while rendering inline bg rgb(242,242,242) (--wash) against the block's rgb(11,61,44). code { background } stopped reading --code-bg when the two backgrounds split on 2026-08-17 and the demo's own words were never updated. Caption and note corrected; the demo function is unchanged and now agrees with what it draws. Four wrong quotes were known; this one was not, and it was a demo contradicting its own render.

CUTS, all deliberate: no CSSDoc.css (framework.css already gives every table max-content + max-width 100% + overflow-x auto - measured, ui/table's width:100% was WORSE, stretching to 2428px at 3440); no page.js and no ext/ children entry (a second cssdoc() call site would contradict 'one call site, one subject' - readme.md is the module's index and links the live demo); no doc/ dir (both traps fit in the readme's Watch out); no specificity column, no doc/style/*.md, no styles: section, no ui/parts.js fix. Property table is LONGHANDS, not the proposal's shorthand names - measured: getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('padding') returns '' in Chrome, so a shorthand row would have had an empty value column. The authored shorthand is in the rule table's declarations cell instead. That is the one place a measurement contradicted the proposal.

v1 landed. Files: ext/CSSDoc/CSSDoc.js (195 lines, 109 of them code - no stylesheet), ext/CSSDoc/readme.md, one line in styles/css-scopes.txt (cssdoc- reserves the namespace; .cssdoc-report/.cssdoc-rules/.cssdoc-props are test hooks, no CSS behind them), and styles/elements/code/page.js (the call site plus five corrections). shot.png is the page at 1280, full height. Also appended one line each to the layout and css skills' improvements.md: layout Q1 never mentions that catalog() moves content() into a child page, so .wide buys the DETAIL column (591px at 1280), not the region.

REVIEW CATCH: cssdoc(target) does not generalise — code(target) builds a <code> element with target as its TEXT, so both specimens are always <code> and cssdoc('blockquote') would silently document code. Output is correct for code; the signature is not. Documented in CSSDoc.js and the readme rather than renamed: generalising needs each element's two contexts chosen, which is v2 design. The builder's 'no second call site' instinct was right for a better reason than it gave.

assign.outcome:
**CSSDoc v1 ships: every CSS rule that lands on an element, read live from the CSSOM, and it catches tonight's bug on sight.**

![](/framework/ai/2026-08-18/cssdoc/shot.png)

Open [**styles/elements/code**](/framework/styles/elements/code/) — *8 rules land on `code`*, in document order, with layer, file, selector and declarations. The `box-shadow` row, verified independently by the mastermind at 1280:

| property | inline | set by | block | set by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| box-shadow | `rgb(230, 230, 230) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset` | `code` | `none` | `code · pre > code` |

One rule inline, **two** in a `pre`. Tonight's defect was the case where the second number is still one — so the page that now exists would have shown it at a glance. Nothing in the tables is typed; a human writes only *why*.

**Why it was needed, proven not argued.** [`styles/elements/code`](/framework/styles/elements/code/) already claimed to render "every element the framework styles, beside the rule that styles it" — and **five** of its hand-copied facts were wrong, including quoting `pre > code { padding: 0; background: none }`, missing the exact declaration that broke. A sixth was a demo captioned against what it drew. All corrected.

- [**The design**](/framework/ai/2026-08-18/cssdoc/proposal.md) — five verdicts, each measured against 1305 live rules. It refuted a `Doc` tab (every `styles/` page is a plain `Page`) and refuted a specificity calculator (`getComputedStyle` *is* the resolved cascade).
- [**The module**](/framework/ext/CSSDoc/readme.md) — 195 lines, no stylesheet, indexed from [`ext/readme.md`](/framework/ext/).
- **A linter cannot replace it.** Three static passes over the CSSOM gave 149 → 74 → 12 candidates and every survivor was an intentional override. Intent is not in the CSSOM. Do not build the linter.
- [**anonymous-sheets.md**](/framework/ai/2026-08-18/cssdoc/anonymous-sheets.md) — 14 of 72 sheets cannot name their file (`ui/parts.js` appends a bare `<style>`). One-argument fix, **34 caller files** — the owner's call, and the recommendation is to do nothing yet.

**Left, deliberately:** `cssdoc(target)` does **not** generalise — both specimens are always a real `<code>`, so `cssdoc("blockquote")` would silently document `code`. Documented in the source and the readme rather than renamed, because generalising means choosing each element's two contexts, which is a v2 design. No `page.js` for the module yet (CLAUDE.md wants one; a second call site is meaningless until it generalises) — the readme is linked from `ext/` meanwhile. No prose files, no `Doc` section, no specificity column.
